sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between the two interpretations of "he took from the stones of the place" and how the power of Israel to make the world a dwelling place for Him comes from the level of Yechidah.

translations.translation: And this is the connection of the two explanations of "and he took from the stones of the place, etc."
[The service in the aspect of the inanimate within man,
and the service of refining the physical things of the world so that they become a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He],
for the power that Israel has to make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,
for the Singular One of the world
[by making from the stones of the place of the world
(stones in the plural)
that they become one stone.
This is the matter of drawing down that Hashem is One,
that even in the heavens and the earth and the four directions of the world
despite them being an aspect of division and separation,
nevertheless, through the revelation of the Aluf of the world
(Aleph=101)
they become unified in true oneness,
that this oneness
(of Hashem is One)
is like Yachid],
is from the aspect of his Yechidah,
which receives
from Yachid.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses how the awakening of the Yechidah and the power of mesirus nefesh, even when initially in a state of poverty, ultimately brings about the revelation of inner powers and leads to wealth in both knowledge and physical matters.

translations.translation: י)
ג)
And behold, even though the awakening of the Yechidah and the power of mesirus nefesh is
(generally)
through the service of the aspect of the inanimate,
namely when a person is in a state of poverty
(in knowledge),
that the inner powers of the Nefesh HaElokis are in concealment and he has no comprehension or feeling of G-dliness
(as above in section 12),
nevertheless,
after he arouses the power of mesirus nefesh while in a state of poverty,
this also brings about the revelation of the inner powers of the Nefesh HaElokis.
And analogous to the promise of our Sages,
"Whoever fulfills the Torah from poverty, his end is to fulfill it from wealth,"
wealth in knowledge,
and also wealth
(and expansion)
in physical matters,
in children, life, and sustenance
(and in all of them)
with abundance
[To the extent that the wealth and expansion in his physical matters is in abundance and tranquility beyond measure and limitation,
for then this wealth itself brings about wealth in knowledge,
because even the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis grasps that such great wealth
(beyond measure and limitation)
can only come from Hashem, the source of all blessings],
and even then his manner of service is with mesirus nefesh beyond intellect.
For this is the explanation of "Whoever fulfills the Torah from poverty, his end is to fulfill it from wealth,"
that he fulfills it from wealth in that same elevation
(mesirus nefesh beyond limitation)
as he fulfilled it from poverty.
This is the matter of "with all your might"
which comes after "with all your heart and with all your soul,"
that is,
that the matter of mesirus nefesh
(beyond intellect)
in "with all your might" is not because of a lack, G-d forbid, in the comprehension of his intellect,
but rather,
that even though his service is with all the powers of his soul
(with all your soul)
the first of which is the power of intellect,
to the extent that this is even grasped by the intellect of his Nefesh HaBahamis
(with all your heart, with both your inclinations),
nevertheless his service is with mesirus nefesh beyond the limitation of intellect,
"with all your might."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through the service of "with all your might," one reaches the true level of "very, very," as with Yaakov, bringing about expansion in both spiritual and physical matters.

translations.translation: And this is also what is said about Yaakov
[from which it is understood,
that so it is also with every Jew],
after his service in the refinement of Lavan's sheep
(the main refinement is in the sheep),
"and the man spread out very, very much, etc."
[very simply,
beyond the aspect of "your might"],
for through the service of the aspect of "with all your might"
(your might)
one reaches the aspect of the true "very."
And it says "very, very"
(twice),
for through the service of "with all your might" being in addition to the encompassing light of Chayah, also from the encompassing light of Yechidah,
through this, the drawing down from above is also "very, very" twice,
the aspect of Arich and also the aspect of Atik.
And a verse does not depart from its simple meaning,
that "and the man spread out very, very much"
(and he had many sheep, etc.)
is
(also)
in the physical,
for through the service of "with all your might,"
he does the will of the Place,
meaning that he
(beyond the aspect of the will of the Place)
does the Will,
including also the explanation of "does" from the term "they compel" regarding charity,
that he compels, as it were, the Will,
"a righteous person decrees and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills," as it is said,
"And you shall decree a thing and it will be established for you,"
[and moreover, the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees and the righteous person annuls],
that he becomes a master over his entire portion in the world,
that he will have expansion in all his matters,
both in spiritual matters and in physical matters,
good in abundance of blessing, in abundance of peace,
wealth in spirituality and wealth in physicality,
and in physicality and spirituality together.
